objective:
Build the RECORD-AND-REPLAY half of the semantic regression corpus: a recording file format that captures what an AI model answered for every corpus case, and a JVM replay that pushes those recorded answers through the REAL domain pipeline and scores them. This is test infrastructure in `core-testing`; no production behaviour changes.

WHY. The real model (Gemini Nano) runs only on a phone, in the foreground, and the owner's phone is rarely available. So the one non-deterministic step -- the model's answer -- is recorded once (by a phone test in SR1.3, or a local stand-in model in SR1.4), and EVERYTHING downstream of it (candidate shortlist, validation, confidence policy, temporal resolution, the capture outcome) is replayed on the JVM on every build. Your replay is what makes the recordings meaningful.

WHAT EXISTS (read the code, do not guess): the corpus from SR1.1 in `core-testing/src/main/kotlin/com/mcfrenchpants/activityledger/core/testing/corpus/` -- `SemanticCorpus` (`load()`, `parse(bytes)`, `sha256`, `cases`, `case(id)`, `catalogFor(case): List<CatalogActivity>` with FIXED ids like `act-mow-lawn`), `CorpusCase` (id, category, catalog, rawText, capturedAt, zoneId, expected, note, knownResolverGap; `capturedInstant`, `zone`), `ExpectedInterpretation` (resolution + allowedResolutions -> `acceptableResolutions`; activityId; newActivityName + allowedNewNames -> `acceptableNewNames`; `allowedStates: List<ActivityState?>` -- a null entry means 'model left state empty' is acceptable; temporalExpression + allowedTemporalExpressions -> `acceptableTemporalExpressions`; `expectedLocalDate`, `precision`; `mustNotMatch`; `outcome` AUTO_ACCEPT/NEEDS_REVIEW), `CorpusCategory`, `ExpectedOutcome`. core-domain: `CandidateSelector`, `TemporalResolver`, `InterpretationValidator`, `CaptureInterpretationOrchestrator(repository, interpreter, clock, selector, resolver, validator)` whose `process(captureId)` returns `AutoAccepted(occurrenceId)` / `NeedsReview(reasons)` / `Rejected(reasons)` / `InterpreterUnavailable(kind)` / `AlreadyHasOccurrence`; `InterpretationCandidate`, `InterpretationInput`, `InterpretationResult.Success/Failure`, `InterpreterFailureKind`, `InterpreterProvenance`; `CaptureSource.PHONE_TEXT`. core-testing: `InMemoryActivityRepository` (`seedActivity(displayName, status, aliases)` generates ids), `FakeActivityInterpreter` (`enqueue`, `respondWith`, settable `provenance`), `MutableClock`, `runSuspend`. The validator auto-accepts only confidence HIGH, rejects a missing state (STATE_MISSING), and new-activity names can auto-accept.

BUILD, in `core-testing/src/main/kotlin/com/mcfrenchpants/activityledger/core/testing/corpus/` unless stated:

1. **Shared input builder.** One function that, for a corpus case, returns the `CandidateSelection` (via the real `CandidateSelector` over `catalogFor(case)`) and the `InterpretationInput(rawText, capturedInstant, zone, selection.candidates)`. The phone recorder (SR1.3) and the stand-in recorder (SR1.4) will both call this, so all three agree byte-for-byte on what the model was shown.

2. **Recording format** (`@Serializable`, kotlinx.serialization is already applied to core-testing; stable, documented, versioned with its own `formatVersion`). Header/provenance: `source` (DEVICE, STAND_IN, SYNTHETIC), `modelLabel`, `deviceModel` (nullable), `interpreterVersion`, `promptVersion`, `schemaVersion`, `corpusSha256`, `recordedAt` (ISO instant), free-text `notes` (nullable, e.g. to record that the stand-in's schema rendering is an approximation). One entry per case: `caseId`, `offeredCandidateIds`, `contextHash`, EITHER an `answer` carrying the seven `InterpretationCandidate` fields (enum fields as their constant names; nullable where the domain type is) OR a `failureKind` (InterpreterFailureKind name), and `latencyMs` (nullable). Provide read (from String/InputStream) and write (to String/OutputStream) functions usable from plain JVM AND from an Android instrumented test (no java.nio.file-only APIs in the write path; take an OutputStream). Also a builder that creates an entry from an `InterpretationResult` + the case's selection + latency, so recorders cannot get the mapping wrong. The recording holds only synthetic corpus-derived data; do not add any field for raw model text.

3. **Test-support change.** Give `InMemoryActivityRepository.seedActivity` an optional explicit `id: String? = null` parameter (default behaviour unchanged) so replay can seed the corpus's fixed ids. Keep its existing tests green; add one for the explicit id.

4. **Replay scorer.** For each recording entry: find the corpus case (unknown case id => the recording is stale: fail loudly); seed a FRESH `InMemoryActivityRepository` with `catalogFor(case)` using the fixed ids; create the capture through the repository API (source PHONE_TEXT, the case's rawText, capturedInstant, zone, speechConfidence null, the processing state a fresh capture uses -- read how the orchestrator tests do it); feed the recorded answer (or failure) through a `FakeActivityInterpreter` whose provenance is the recording's; run the REAL `CaptureInterpretationOrchestrator` with the default real selector/resolver/validator and a fixed clock; then read back the outcome and any occurrence/activity from the repository. Before scoring, assert the replayed selection's `contextHash` and candidate ids equal the recorded ones; a mismatch means the recording no longer matches the corpus -- fail loudly naming the case id. Do NOT re-implement any domain rule in the harness: the classification below reads results, it does not re-decide them.

   Classify each entry into exactly one class:
   - NOT_RUN: recorded failure UNAVAILABLE or RETRYABLE (infrastructure, not model quality); excluded from rates, counted separately.
   - CORRECT: expected NEEDS_REVIEW and no occurrence was created (NeedsReview, Rejected, or a MALFORMED/OTHER failure all count as 'went to review'); OR expected AUTO_ACCEPT and the outcome is AutoAccepted AND the occurrence's activity is right (existing: equals expected activityId; new: a newly created activity whose NameNormalizer-normalized name is in the normalized `acceptableNewNames`, and not any existing catalog activity), its state is in `allowedStates`, and -- when the case has an expected time -- its occurredAt local date (case zone) and precision match.
   - SAFE_MISS: expected AUTO_ACCEPT but nothing was saved (review / rejected / malformed / other). The user would be asked; nothing wrong is recorded. Include the validation reasons.
   - UNSAFE_MISS: an occurrence was created and ANY of: expected NEEDS_REVIEW; activity is in `mustNotMatch`; wrong existing activity; a NEW activity created when an existing one was expected (a duplicate); an existing one matched when new was expected; state not allowed; wrong date or precision. Include which check failed.
   Also record, per entry, secondary diagnostics that do not change the class: whether the recorded resolution is in `acceptableResolutions`, whether the recorded temporalExpression is in `acceptableTemporalExpressions` (compare trimmed, case-insensitive), the recorded confidence band, the validation reasons, latency.

5. **Report.** A pure function from scored results + provenance to Markdown, plus a short plain-text console summary. Markdown sections: provenance header (with a prominent 'STAND-IN MODEL -- NOT THE OFFICIAL RESULT' banner when source is STAND_IN, and similarly for SYNTHETIC); totals per class; per-category table; every UNSAFE_MISS then every SAFE_MISS with case id, category, what went wrong and the reasons; confidence band vs class table (for calibrating the auto-accept policy); temporal-expression agreement count; latency median and max when present; list of NOT_RUN ids. Case ids and short reason codes only -- do NOT put raw corpus sentences or model output text in the console summary (the Markdown may include the case's rawText for readability, since the corpus is synthetic and committed; do not include proposed names beyond the class reason).

6. **Replay tests + regression gate** in `core-testing/src/test/kotlin/com/mcfrenchpants/activityledger/core/testing/corpus/`, with recordings under `core-testing/src/test/resources/semantic-corpus/recordings/`:
   a. Scorer self-tests driven by a small committed SYNTHETIC recording (source SYNTHETIC, a clearly synthetic file name, a handful of entries against real corpus cases) or by entries built in code: one each of CORRECT existing match, CORRECT new activity, CORRECT review, SAFE_MISS (a MEDIUM-confidence answer demoted to review), UNSAFE_MISS via mustNotMatch, UNSAFE_MISS via duplicate new activity, UNSAFE_MISS via wrong date, NOT_RUN, a MALFORMED failure, and a stale recording (wrong contextHash, and unknown case id) failing loudly.
   b. Recording round-trip: write then read gives an equal recording; builder-from-InterpretationResult maps every field.
   c. The gate test: if `recordings/device-latest.json` exists, replay it, write the Markdown report to `core-testing/build/reports/semantic-corpus/device.md`, print the console summary, and FAIL if any case id listed in `recordings/baseline.json` (a simple JSON list of case ids, format documented) is not CORRECT -- naming the case ids. Also fail if the recording's corpusSha256 differs from the current corpus AND any baseline case is missing from the recording. If `recordings/standin-latest.json` exists, replay it and write `standin.md` + summary, NEVER failing on its scores (only on a malformed/stale file). Missing recording or baseline files => the test is SKIPPED via JUnit Assume with a message saying none has been recorded yet (none exist yet; the first real ones come in later tasks). Do NOT commit a fake device-latest.json or baseline.json.
   d. Make it easy for later scripts to run only the replay: put the gate in its own test class and note its fully-qualified name in your report (later tasks run `./gradlew :core-testing:test --tests <that class>`). Ensure the report is written even when the gate then fails.

STANDING RULES. Test infrastructure only: no change to core-domain, core-data, core-ai, app-phone, app-wear. Needing a production change is `scope_change_requested`. No domain rule duplicated in the harness (AGENTS.md #5 / ADR-010: model output only ever reaches storage through the real validator -- the replay must go through it too). No printing of corpus sentences or model output to the console beyond case ids and reason codes. Kotlin stays 2.3.21; no new libraries beyond what core-testing already has (kotlinx-serialization, kotlin-test, core-domain).
non_goals: No phone/instrumented recorder, no stand-in model client, no scripts (SR1.3, SR1.4).
No real device or stand-in recording and no baseline.json -- those come from real runs later.
No change to the corpus cases or to SR1.1's tests, except where the model API needs a small compatible addition; any change to an expected value is out of scope.
No change to any production module, the prompt, the validator or the confidence policy.
Do not disable, @Ignore or weaken any existing test. Do not commit.
acceptance_criteria: A single shared function builds a case's CandidateSelection and InterpretationInput using the real CandidateSelector over catalogFor(case); the replay uses it.

A versioned, documented recording format exists with provenance (source DEVICE/STAND_IN/SYNTHETIC, modelLabel, deviceModel, interpreter/prompt/schema versions, corpusSha256, recordedAt, notes) and per-case entries (caseId, offeredCandidateIds, contextHash, answer-or-failureKind, latencyMs); read/write work from an OutputStream/InputStream; a builder maps InterpretationResult + selection + latency to an entry; round-trip test passes.
InMemoryActivityRepository.seedActivity accepts an optional explicit id with unchanged default behaviour, covered by a test.

Replay runs each entry through the REAL CaptureInterpretationOrchestrator with real selector, resolver and validator via FakeActivityInterpreter and a fresh InMemoryActivityRepository seeded with the fixed ids; grep of the harness shows no re-implementation of validation, confidence or temporal rules.
Replay fails loudly, naming the case, on an unknown case id or a contextHash/candidate-id mismatch.

Every entry is classified into exactly one of NOT_RUN, CORRECT, SAFE_MISS, UNSAFE_MISS per the packet's rules, with secondary diagnostics recorded; scorer self-tests cover each listed scenario and all pass.
Markdown report and console summary are generated with every listed section; STAND_IN and SYNTHETIC are bannered as not official; console output contains only case ids, counts and reason codes.

Gate test: replays device-latest.json when present, writes build/reports/semantic-corpus/device.md, fails naming any baseline case id that is not CORRECT; stand-in replay never fails on scores; missing files => Assume-skip with a clear message. No device-latest.json or baseline.json is committed. The gate's fully-qualified class name is in the report.
No file outside write_paths changed; no production module changed.
